theme: FX and purchasing power: exchange-rate history (ECB, BIS, FRED), broad-dollar indices, PPP/Big Mac, tourist affordability indices, company FX-exposure tooling
queries_run: gh search repos "big mac index" --sort stars
gh search repos "ECB exchange rate" --sort stars
gh search repos "ECB exchange rates dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "dollar index dxy dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "BIS effective exchange rate" --sort stars
gh search repos "purchasing power parity dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "fx exposure hedging" --sort stars
gh search repos "FRED exchange rate python" --sort stars

candidates.name: TheEconomist/big-mac-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Economist Big Mac Index source data and methodology, MIT licensed, 1748 stars, updated same day as our search (13 Sep 2026, actively maintained). Three committed files: big-mac-raw-index.csv, big-mac-adjusted-index.csv (GDP-adjusted), big-mac-full-index.csv, each carrying underlying local prices, exchange rates and implied-vs-actual PPP by country. Biannual since ~2000, ~70 countries incl. all ABNB's major regions (EU, UK, Japan, Australia, Mexico, Brazil, India). July 2022 methodology change archived in Releases so old vintage is recoverable.
candidates.why_useful: Direct, long-running, free PPP/affordability series by country -> usable as a cross-check on real (purchasing-power-adjusted) ADR moves and as an affordability proxy for inbound/outbound travel demand by region (gap #6 consumer spend / broader macro-consumer-spend theme, and general FX/PPP gap not separately numbered but explicitly requested by this theme). Also a clean point-in-time-able series since each release is dated and archived.
candidates.time_coverage: ~2000-present, semiannual (Jan/Jul), with July 2022 methodology break archived separately
candidates.size_hint: 3 CSVs, small (~tens of KB), full history

candidates.name: AllRates-Today/ecb-exchange-rate
candidates.what_it_holds: Zero-dependency Node.js/TypeScript client wrapping the ECB's official daily reference-rate feed: ~41 currencies vs EUR, full history back to 1999 (ECB's own published range). No data files committed beyond the client code; it re-fetches from ECB's public XML feed on demand.
candidates.why_useful: One-command pull for daily EUR cross-rates since 1999 covering all of ABNB's EMEA-relevant currencies (GBP, and via cross-rates most others); useful for building our own point-in-time FX vintage register (rule #2 in our own CLAUDE.md) since ECB rates are date-stamped at source.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold FX schedules per CONTEXT.md; this is a possibly-longer/cleaner daily-since-1999 acquisition method worth flagging per the 'better/longer/older' rule.

candidates.name: cyanheads/exchange-rates-mcp-server
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server (STDIO/HTTP) for currency conversion, FX rates, and querying historical ECB exchange-rate data. Apache-2.0. Actively updated (12 Sep 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Alternative machine-callable historical ECB FX puller (could be dropped into an agent tool chain instead of hand-rolling XML parsing); marginal beyond the plain client above but notable as a maintained, typed access layer with explicit 'historical' query support.
candidates.time_coverage: historical ECB range (1999-present per ECB feed)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps with AllRates-Today client above; flagged as an alternative tool, not new data.

candidates.name: dillonsnyman1/fx-exposure-hedging-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Dashboard/tool that calculates FX portfolio exposure, models forward hedging via covered interest rate parity, computes currency-level VaR and hedge effectiveness. No committed historical dataset found (student/portfolio project, 0 stars, updated Jul 2026); needs its own rate inputs.
candidates.why_useful: Could serve as a template/regression method for estimating how much of ABNB's revenue/EBITDA translation exposure to EUR/GBP/etc. is hedge-able or historically has moved with spot, i.e. an FX-exposure regression tool as hinted in the task's keywords. Not a data source itself.

candidates.name: yalerong/FX-Hedge-Lab
candidates.what_it_holds: 'Local FX exposure, hedging, scenario PnL, and backtesting workbench' — a methods/tooling repo (0 stars, updated 5 Sep 2026, no license stated). No dataset confirmed committed; likely a scenario-modeling scaffold.
candidates.why_useful: Same family as the FX exposure/hedging tooling keyword hint; potentially adaptable as a scenario-PnL framework for stress-testing ABNB's FX translation sensitivity (EUR/GBP mix, per the FX-line-swap bridge work already in our repo) but is a generic tool, not ABNB- or travel-specific data.

candidates.name: greven/forex
candidates.what_it_holds: Elixir library for ECB exchange rates, MIT licensed, actively updated (10 Sep 2026). Wraps the same ECB daily feed as other clients; no separate stored dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal alternative client to the ECB feed; listed for completeness of the 'method' landscape, not because it adds new data beyond what ECB itself and other clients already expose.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Duplicate of AllRates-Today client in function; different language binding only.

notes: Big Mac index (TheEconomist/big-mac-data) is the clear high-value find for this theme — well-maintained, MIT, long history, GDP-adjusted PPP by country, directly usable as an affordability/FX cross-check. Direct gh search hits for 'BIS effective exchange rate', 'purchasing power parity dataset', 'dollar index dxy dataset', and 'FRED exchange rate python' all returned zero results — GitHub's repo search does not match on these longer/more specific phrases well; a code-search or WebSearch pass (not used here per the 10/min gh search code cap and to conserve the 6-call gh search budget) would likely surface more (e.g. FRED API python wrappers like fredapi/full-fred are well known off-platform but did not surface via these exact phrasings; BIS effective exchange rate series does not appear to have a popular GitHub mirror). ECB exchange-rate searches surfaced only thin API-client wrappers (all re-fetching from ECB's public 1999-present feed, no committed historical CSVs) — none of these hold a broad-dollar or Fed nominal/real trade-weighted index, which remains an open gap for a future scout to search directly (terms: 'Fed nominal broad dollar index', 'FRED DTWEXBGS', 'trade weighted dollar index github'). No tourist-affordability-index-specific repo was found under these search terms; worth a follow-up search on 'travel affordability index' or 'cost of travel index dataset'. All 6 permitted gh search calls were used; stopped searching per budget rather than exhausting all keyword variants.
